title: Pricing 517 Hickorywood Ave
subtitle: Listing Presentation · Altamonte Springs, Spring Oaks
recommendation_why: It sits at the middle of what recent sales support and gives you the strongest launch, when buyer attention is highest.
value_drivers: The single biggest reason your home sells near the top of the neighborhood.
Worth about $25,000 against similar homes without one.
Four Bedrooms, No HOA or CDD
Flexible space and no monthly association costs.
Flood insurance isn't required, which keeps buyers' costs down.
document_items: Permit and date. Roof age decides whether a buyer can insure the home.
Kitchen, bath, electrical, and plumbing work. Undocumented upgrades count for less.

comp_lines.622 Spring Oaks Blvd: Renovated pool home; April, before rates rose
comp_lines.516 Oakwood Ct: Same year and size; systems documented
comp_lines.745 Little Wekiva Cir: Most recent pool sale; not renovated

comps_takeaway: The two highest sold in the spring. The recent sales point to the middle of the range.
scatter_takeaway: Renovated pool homes sell well above the neighborhood trend. At {list_price}, yours sits among them without testing the ceiling.
market_takeaway: Buyers are negotiating again. Price for the market we have now, not the one from April.
competition: Renovated, same size, no pool. The value alternative buyers will tour.
Renovated pool home. Priced right, it sold fast.
Updated pool home. Priced above the market, and sitting.
competition_takeaway: Well-priced renovated pool homes are moving. Overpriced ones sit.
strategy_takeaway: All three net within a few thousand dollars. The real choice is time and risk.
payment_takeaway: Buyers shop by payment. Every $10,000 is about {per_10k} a month to them.
launch_plan: Permit and date, ready to share
Decide it now, before offers arrive
Steady showings but no offer? Revisit the price
needs_short: Roof permit and date, plus any 4-point or wind-mitigation report
Ages of AC, water heater, and pool equipment
Anything known about leaks, claims, or repairs
Your estimated mortgage payoff and target closing date
adjustments_summary: Adjustments: about $75 per sq ft of size difference; $30,000–$45,000 for renovation level; $5,000–$10,000 for larger or better lots; 1–2% for market change since the sale; seller-paid costs subtracted.

notes.recommendation: Lead with the answer. The rest of the presentation shows how we got here.
notes.method: 35 sales within a mile since April; we kept the 5 closest in size, pool, age and neighborhood, adjusted each for differences from your home, and the median adjusted value is about $469,800.
notes.drivers: These are the features the adjustments credit your home for. The roof and permits need paperwork before buyers and appraisers will pay for them.
notes.comps: Each bar is what that home would have sold for if it were yours. Adjustment details are in the report and the appendix.
notes.scatter: Every sale and listing within a mile. The dotted line is size alone; renovation and pool push homes above it.
notes.market: Spring = April to June sales; summer = July to mid-September. Rates are the Freddie Mac 30-year average.
notes.competition: These are the homes a buyer will likely tour alongside yours.
notes.strategies: Expected sale prices and timelines are estimates from recent sales. The $459,900 option assumes competing offers reduce the seller credit to $5,000.
notes.nets: Before mortgage payoff. Brokerage is a 2.5% + 2.5% placeholder until we finalize the listing agreement.
notes.payments: Conventional loan, 5% down, 6.95%, city taxes with homestead, $3,600 insurance, 0.5% PMI.
notes.launch: Low-cost steps that remove the questions that cost sellers money at the negotiating table.
notes.next: Confirm the documents and the launch date.
